issue.title: AI CLI
issue.bodyHtml:
Description

Use AI SDK to run command against LLMs. See https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/ for inspiration.

AI SDK Version

No response

comment.bodyHtml:
• Files support – make it really easy to attach a bunch of files, upload transparently
  • Easy model switching - e.g.: -m to alternate between models
  • Unix-y - make it easy to pipe, consume stdin, etc. e.g.: echo 'what is life?' | npx ai

long.bodyHtml:
• Structured output, so it can be used as code, composable.

Usage

$ curl -s https://acme.com/pricing | \
  npx ai "extract pricing tiers" --schema '{
    "tiers": [{
      "name": "string",
      "price": "number",
      "bandwidth_gb": "number",
      "team_members": "number"
    }]
  }'

Output:

{
  "tiers": [
    {"name": "Starter", "price": 0, "bandwidth_gb": 50, "team_members": 1},
    {"name": "Growth", "price": 29, "bandwidth_gb": 500, "team_members": 5},
    {"name": "Scale", "price": 99, "bandwidth_gb": 2000, "team_members": 20},
    {"name": "Enterprise", "price": -1, "bandwidth_gb": -1, "team_members": -1}
  ]
}

Advanced usage – solving harder problems with AI as an API blackbox

Ex: Installing the latest version of a github release is trickier than it may seem, but it could become something like:

#!/bin/bash
# install-latest.sh - Install any GitHub CLI tool with one command

REPO=$1  # e.g., "junegunn/fzf"

# Get latest release data
curl -s "https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/releases/latest" | \
  npx ai "find download URL for $(uname -s) $(uname -m)" --schema '{
    "download_url": "string",
    "binary_name": "string",
    "extract_command": "string"
  }' > release.json

# Extract the info
URL=$(jq -r .download_url release.json)
BINARY=$(jq -r .binary_name release.json)
EXTRACT=$(jq -r .extract_command release.json)

# Download and install
curl -L "$URL" -o /tmp/download
eval "$EXTRACT” # 🤠
chmod +x "$BINARY"
sudo mv "$BINARY" /usr/local/bin/

echo "✓ Installed $BINARY”

Usage

# Install fzf (handles .tar.gz)
$ ./install-latest.sh junegunn/fzf
✓ Installed fzf

# Install ripgrep (handles different naming: rg)
$ ./install-latest.sh BurntSushi/ripgrep  
✓ Installed rg

pr.title: feat(cli): add ai command line interface
pr.bodyHtml:
background

We wanted to make it simple to use AI from the command line without having to write code or learn APIs.

summary

  • add ai cli with file attachment support
  • add model switching via -m flag
  • add unix-style piping and stdin support

verification

  • cli handles text and image file attachments
  • model switching works across providers (openai, anthropic, groq, etc.)
  • stdin piping works with echo, cat, curl commands
  • authentication via VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN and AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
  • verbose mode shows usage statistics

tasks

  • cli argument parsing with model, file, system options
  • file attachment with mime type detection
  • stdin reading for unix piping
  • gateway provider integration
  • image file base64 encoding
  • streaming text output
  • error handling and help documentation
